sources.title: Santander - Program Sheet - 060126.pdf
sources.read_as: 300 dpi render, all 11 pages rendered. This proposal is built from pages 1 and 2, which carry the program tables and contract rules. Pages 3-11 are stipulation and income documentation detail that the record's existing id and income sections already reflect; they were not re-extracted.

Up to 75 mo84 mo

Vehicle ageNew to 12 yearsNew to 5 years

changes.quote: Max Term | Up to 75 Months | 84 Months · Max LTV | Up to 145% | 115% front, 120% back · Max Mileage | 150,000 | 60,000
changes.note: Santander had no LTV section at all. The 84-month column is the point: it is not simply a longer version of the 75-month program. LTV drops from 145% to 115% front and 120% back, mileage from 150,000 to 60,000, vehicle age from 12 years to 5, and the minimum frontend advance triples from $5,000 to $15,000. The record advertised maxTerm 84 and maxMileage 150,000 side by side, which are the two columns that never apply together.

new.label: Backend Products
new.content:
GAP$1,200 or the state maximum, whichever is less
Vehicle Service ContractUp to $6,500
Backend AllowanceSubject to state maximums and varies by approval — check the callback

changes.quote: Vehicle service contracts up to $6,500 · GAP $1,200 or max permitted by state law, if less
changes.note: No backend section existed. The $6,500 VSC ceiling is high relative to the rest of the book and was recorded nowhere — the record only carried GAP at $1,200 as a scalar field.

new.label: Reserve & Compensation
new.content:
ParticipationUp to 2.5% (12–60 mo) · 2% (61–75 mo) · 1.5% (76–84 mo)
Split75/25, ratio method: (dealer part ÷ contract rate) × total finance charge × split
Rate BuydownDealer may buy the rate down up to 3 points, but never below base rate
Dealer FeesAs low as $0 — a contract assignment fee may still apply
Expired Approval$495 to re-approve a deal that expired before funding

Flat scale — written at buy rate

Amount financedFlat
$10,000–$14,999$100
$15,000–$19,999$150
$20,000–$24,999$200
$25,000–$29,999$250
$30,000–$34,999$300
$35,000–$75,999$350

changes.note: No reserve section existed — compensation was one sentence in a scalar field saying "flat option up to $350". The actual scale is six brackets, and $350 only arrives at $35,000 financed. Also adds the rate buydown (up to 3 points, never below base) and the ratio-method participation formula.

new.label: Vehicle Eligibility
new.content:
Max Vehicle Age12 years (5 years on an 84-month term)
Max Mileage150,000 (60,000 on an 84-month term)
Commercial UnitsMay still be eligible through the Small Business Auto channel
🚫Ineligible: RVs, exotics, motorcycles, boats, ATVs, van conversions, trailers, right-hand drive, hail damage, vehicles from defunct manufacturers, gray market, frame damage, salvaged or reconditioned titles, and commercial use — livery, delivery, taxi, and ride-share (Uber, Lyft, Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub).

changes.quote: Ineligible vehicles include but are not limited to recreational vehicles, exotics, motorcycles, boats, all-terrain vehicles, van conversions, trailers, right-hand drive, hail damage
changes.note: Santander had no vehicles section, so the page carried no ineligible list at all — the one thing a desk checks before wasting a submission. Note the exit at the end: commercial, livery and delivery units may still go through the Small Business Auto channel rather than being a flat decline.

ambiguities.note: Record says "See callback" and the record itself carries a warning that this is a new lender whose chargeback window and bureau should be confirmed with the rep. Pages 1-2 state no chargeback policy, so that warning still stands and I have not removed it.

Pages 3-11 were rendered but not re-extracted line by line. They are the stipulation guidelines and the W-2 / self-employed / 1099 / other-taxable / non-taxable income document rules, which the record's id and income sections already cover in detail. If you want those verified rather than assumed, say so and I will do a second pass on this lender.
